ops.statement: When a run's acceptance depends on launching headless agents (e.g. claude -p) that must DO work (write files, drive a spine), probe the headless PERMISSION MODEL at the feasibility step, not just CLI presence/auth: run a trivial headless FILE-WRITE ("create hello.txt and stop") and confirm the file appears. A headless claude -p has no interactive approver, so tool actions needing approval are silently denied and the agent produces nothing — which only surfaces as a false-red at the acceptance gate if you probed only `claude --version`/`claude -p 'say ok'`.
ops.grounding: .agent-work/issue-106/acceptance.md — the g5 live run (7 min, completed-fail) transcript shows the headless agent permission-denied on Write/Bash-redirection/PowerShell; the understand-step probe passed on version+echo but missed the write-permission block, deferring the honest-null 4 gates.
ops.target: the commander feasibility-probe habit at understand (for headless-agent-tool runs, add a trivial headless file-write probe)
